candidates.name: Test-Json
verified_facts: Test-Json validates JSON syntax and can validate against a schema string or schema file
LiteralPath permits exact file-path handling
semantic_limits: Schema validity does not prove receipt freshness, producer identity, Git publication, or semantic truth

candidates.name: about_Output_Streams
verified_facts: PowerShell has distinct success, error, warning, verbose, debug, information, and progress streams
The progress stream is not redirectable
semantic_limits: A quiet success stream does not prove that warning, error, information, or native stderr streams were empty

candidates.name: about_Redirection
verified_facts: PowerShell redirection can route numbered streams and all streams to files
PowerShell 7.4 preserves native stdout byte streams when redirected directly
semantic_limits: Combining native stderr with stdout converts the combined stream to string data and is unsuitable for binary fidelity

candidates.name: about_CommonParameters
verified_facts: Common parameters include ErrorAction, ErrorVariable, WarningVariable, InformationVariable, OutVariable, and ProgressAction
Command-scoped common parameters override broader preferences for that invocation
semantic_limits: Common parameters do not replace native exit-code capture or post-command receipt validation

candidates.name: about_Parsing
verified_facts: PowerShell uses expression mode and argument mode when parsing commands
Paths and arguments containing spaces require correct quoting and native-command argument behavior can vary by PowerShell version
semantic_limits: Rendered command text alone does not prove the native process received the intended argument vector

candidates.name: about_Quoting_Rules
verified_facts: Single-quoted strings are literal while double-quoted strings can expand variables and expressions
Here-strings support multiline literal or expandable text
semantic_limits: Quoting correctness must be verified against the exact command and data; it does not establish authorization or success

candidates.name: about_Splatting
verified_facts: Splatting passes collections of parameter values to commands as a unit
Hashtable splatting associates keys with named parameters
semantic_limits: Splatting improves deterministic parameter construction but does not validate values, permissions, or command outcomes

candidates.name: Format-Hex
verified_facts: Format-Hex displays byte data and can read exact file paths
Its output can expose byte-order marks and unexpected byte prefixes
semantic_limits: Hex display is diagnostic and does not replace a cryptographic hash or full byte-for-byte comparison

candidates.name: Compare-Object
verified_facts: Compare-Object compares reference and difference object sets
Explicit properties can be selected for comparison
semantic_limits: Default string conversion or an underspecified property list can hide meaningful semantic differences

candidates.name: Measure-Object
verified_facts: Measure-Object calculates counts and numeric aggregates for input objects
Property-based measurement can summarize lengths or sizes
semantic_limits: Aggregate counts and sums do not prove item identity, completeness, uniqueness, or integrity

candidates.name: Get-PSDrive
verified_facts: Get-PSDrive lists PowerShell drives in the current session and exposes their providers and roots
FileSystem drive information can include used and free space
semantic_limits: A PSDrive mapping is session context and does not prove the underlying path is writable or stable

candidates.name: Get-Job
verified_facts: Get-Job retrieves PowerShell jobs in the current session
Job state, identity, location, command, and child jobs can be inspected
semantic_limits: PowerShell job inventory does not enumerate unrelated processes or prove ownership of the canonical runner

candidates.name: Wait-Job
verified_facts: Wait-Job waits for jobs to reach a terminating state
The Timeout parameter bounds the wait
semantic_limits: A completed job can still have failed output or invalid receipts; timeout and state must be recorded

candidates.name: Receive-Job
verified_facts: Receive-Job retrieves job results
Keep can preserve results for subsequent reads and Wait can wait while receiving
semantic_limits: Receiving output does not prove output completeness unless child jobs, streams, state, and errors are also checked

candidates.name: Get-Error
verified_facts: Get-Error displays detailed information about recent PowerShell errors
Specific ErrorRecord objects can be supplied for inspection
semantic_limits: Error detail is diagnostic and can be stale or unrelated unless correlated to the exact command and timestamp

candidates.name: about_Try_Catch_Finally
verified_facts: Try blocks can catch terminating errors and finally blocks run for cleanup
Catch blocks can inspect the current ErrorRecord
semantic_limits: Non-terminating errors require explicit escalation or checking; cleanup execution does not imply successful recovery

candidates.name: git-worktree
verified_facts: git worktree list can enumerate the main and linked worktrees and porcelain output is script-friendly
Worktrees can be locked to prevent automatic pruning
semantic_limits: Listing worktrees does not prove that an external runner is inactive or that a worktree is safe to mutate

candidates.name: git-stash
verified_facts: git stash list and git stash show inspect stored stash entries
Including untracked files requires the corresponding stash option at creation time
semantic_limits: A stash entry must be identified and inspected; its existence alone does not prove every intended file was captured

candidates.name: git-merge-base
verified_facts: git merge-base finds common ancestors between commits
The is-ancestor mode tests whether one commit is an ancestor of another by exit status
semantic_limits: An ancestor relationship does not prove working-tree cleanliness, remote freshness, or successful push

candidates.name: git-rev-list
verified_facts: git rev-list traverses commit objects and supports set operations over revision ranges
Left-right count can summarize unique commits on each side of a symmetric difference
semantic_limits: Commit counts do not prove content equivalence, remote authorization, or receipt validity

candidates.name: git-show-ref
verified_facts: git show-ref lists references and object IDs
Verify and exists modes support exact ref checks with exit status
semantic_limits: Local ref presence does not prove that the corresponding remote ref has the same object ID

candidates.name: git-symbolic-ref
verified_facts: git symbolic-ref reads symbolic references such as HEAD
Quiet mode can suppress normal error output while preserving exit status
semantic_limits: A symbolic HEAD target does not prove its commit is current, pushed, or safe to execute

candidates.name: git-diff
verified_facts: git diff compares working tree, index, trees, commits, blobs, or paths depending on invocation
Exit-code and quiet modes support machine checks for differences
semantic_limits: The exact comparison endpoints and submodule settings must be explicit; empty output can otherwise be misleading

candidates.name: git-diff-files
verified_facts: git diff-files compares working-tree files with the index
Quiet mode implies exit-code behavior and can disable untrusted external diff helpers
semantic_limits: It does not compare untracked files or remote refs and must be combined with other checks

candidates.name: git-ls-files
verified_facts: git ls-files merges index and working-tree information and can select cached, modified, deleted, untracked, ignored, or unmerged paths
Null-delimited output supports safe path parsing
semantic_limits: Selected flags determine visibility; incomplete flag sets can omit important dirty-state classes

candidates.name: git-check-ignore
verified_facts: git check-ignore reports whether paths are excluded by ignore rules
Verbose and non-matching output can expose rule provenance and unmatched paths
semantic_limits: Ignored status does not make a file safe to discard and does not prove it was captured in a stash

candidates.name: git-cat-file
verified_facts: git cat-file can test object existence, report object type and size, or show object contents
Batch modes support efficient scripted object queries
semantic_limits: Object existence in the local database does not prove reachability from the expected ref or remote publication

candidates.name: git-hash-object
verified_facts: git hash-object computes an object ID for file content as Git would store it
Without write mode it can calculate hashes without adding objects
semantic_limits: A matching blob hash proves content identity under the selected object type, not path metadata, execution, or push

candidates.name: git-fetch
verified_facts: git fetch downloads objects and refs and records fetched refs in FETCH_HEAD
Atomic mode updates local refs as one transaction or leaves them unchanged on error
semantic_limits: Fetch mutates local remote-tracking state and must be bounded, targeted, and followed by exact ref readback

candidates.name: git-push
verified_facts: git push updates remote refs and transfers required objects
Dry-run, porcelain, atomic, and explicit refspec options provide safer machine-oriented control
semantic_limits: A local success message is insufficient; the remote ref must be read back and matched to the intended object ID

candidates.name: git-branch
verified_facts: git branch can list local and remote-tracking branches and show current or verbose tracking information
Contains, merged, and points-at filters support branch relationship inspection
semantic_limits: Branch listings are local metadata and do not prove remote freshness or worktree safety

candidates.name: git-reflog
verified_facts: Reflogs record local ref-tip updates and HEAD movement
The show and exists modes support read-only history and presence checks
semantic_limits: Reflogs are local, may expire, and are not evidence that a remote update succeeded
